1.
Heard Sri Vir Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the revisionist and Sri Anurag Pandey, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the revisionist is taken on record.

3. This criminal revision has been filed for setting aside the judgment and order dated 10.10.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Jalaun at Orai and order dated 19.10.2023 passed by the Additional District and Session Judge/Special Judge (Rape with POCSO), Jalaun at Orai in Criminal Appeal No. 53 of 2023 affirming the order of J. J. Board declining bail to the juvenile in case crime no. 164 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S.-Kotwali Kalpi,
District Jalaun.

sentences.text:
an FIR was lodged under section 363 IPC; later on same was converted into Sections 363, 366,
376(3) I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, on the basis of evidence collected; finding involvement of the juvenile in the matter, he was apprehended and finding him as below 18 years, he was produced before the Juvenile Justice Board; his application for release was rejected; the appeal filed challenging the aforesaid order was also rejected; now the juvenile, through his father is before this court in this criminal revision.
The juvenile is in custody since 09.06.2023 i.e., about more than 9 months now.

5. It is contended on behalf of the revisionist that he was found 16 years 5 months on the date of the incident and the girl was found about 15 years; the medical examination report does not corroborate the theory of sexual assault; she in her statement under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., said that she voluntarily went with the accused and she has been in contact with the accused since quite sometime; her statement show that she has been in love relationship with the accused; in such circumstances, no criminal intent can be attributed to the act; it is further submitted that nothing has been found in the social investigation report as regard his behaviour, conduct and antecedents of the accused and therefore the Juvenile Justice Board as well as the appellate court fell in error in declining bail to him.
6. Learned AGA has opposed prayer for bail.
7. I went through the material on record, including the statements given by the alleged victim, the medical examination as well as the social investigation report.

The J.J.Board has declined bail on the basis of the observations that in case he is released, there is possibility that he will be exposed to moral, physical or psychological danger and that he may come in association with some known criminal and that his release would defeat ends of justice.
Learned appellate court seems to have agreed with this observation.

In none of the orders any material has been mentioned on the basis whereof such observations were made bringing the matter within the three exclusionary clauses as provided in proviso to Section 12 of the J.J.Act.

It is settled law that whenever a minor, who is alleged to have committed an offence, is apprehended and produced before the board, he shall be released on bail unless the release is likely to bring him in association with any known criminal or there is likelihood of exposure to moral or psychological danger or that such release would defeat ends of justice.
8.
In view of the above, the revision is allowed.

The judgment and order dated 10.10.2023 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Jalaun at Orai and order dated 19.10.2023 passed by the Additional District and Session Judge/Special Judge (Rape with POCSO), Jalaun at Orai, are hereby set aside.
